canDo: Names and sounds all 28 letters; recognises the four positional forms and knows which six letters (ا د ذ ر ز و) do not join to the letter that follows; reads fully-vowelled CV and CVV syllables aloud.
source: Arabic script-literacy competency (no CEFR analogue); standard first-year sequence, e.g. Al-Kitaab Part 1 Alif Baa; ACTFL Arabic — script and sound system.

canDo: Reads fully-vowelled words and short sentences aloud accurately; correctly handles sukūn, shaddah, the three tanwīn, tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), alif maqṣūra (ى), and sun/moon-letter assimilation of the definite article ال.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension A1, adapted for full vowelling; Arabic reading-mark competency from standard first-year sequences.

canDo: Reads fully-vowelled paragraphs on familiar topics; begins reading high-frequency words that carry only the vowels needed to resolve ambiguity; recognises common word-shape (wazn) patterns.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension A2; the fully→partially vowelled transition is an Arabic-specific stage (documented rationale).

canDo: Reads mostly-unvowelled MSA on familiar and everyday topics, supplying vowels from morphological pattern and context; handles broken plurals and derived-verb forms met in context.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension B1; the unvowelled-reading milestone from ACTFL Arabic — Intermediate Reading.

canDo: Reads unvowelled authentic texts — news reports, feature articles, factual prose — with occasional dictionary support; follows the line of argument and separates main points from detail.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension B2 / Reading for Information and Argument B2.

canDo: Reads editorials, essays, and literary prose fluently; handles register shifts, ellipsis, complex subordination, and implicit meaning; needs the dictionary only for low-frequency or specialised vocabulary.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension C1; ACTFL Arabic — Advanced/Superior Reading.

canDo: Reads virtually any prose — classical and heritage texts, specialised academic and legal writing, sophisticated literary style — parsing structural ambiguity and appreciating stylistic nuance.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Reading Comprehension C2; ACTFL Arabic — Distinguished Reading.

canDo: Forms all 28 letters in isolation with correct stroke order and direction (right-to-left, top-to-bottom); copies fully-vowelled syllables legibly.
notes: Machine-checkable at this level (stroke order, letter-form selection).
source: Arabic handwriting pedagogy (no CEFR analogue); CEFR-CV 2018 Orthographic Control Pre-A1 for the copying element.

canDo: Writes letters correctly in initial / medial / final position with correct joining; spells familiar fully-vowelled words from dictation; writes short simple sentences (subject + predicate).
notes: Joining and dictation machine-checkable; sentence writing self-assessed.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production A1 + Orthographic Control A1.

canDo: Writes a short connected paragraph on a familiar topic (self, family, daily routine) using learned vocabulary and basic connectors (وَ، ثُمَّ، لكِنْ); spelling of high-frequency words is generally accurate.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production A2.

canDo: Writes straightforward connected texts — a description, a narrative, an informal message — on familiar topics; links ideas with common conjunctions and relative clauses; attempts case endings where required.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production B1.

canDo: Writes clear, detailed texts — an argumentative paragraph, a formal message, a summary — with appropriate paragraphing and cohesion; controls the case system and derived forms with occasional slips.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production B2 + Grammatical Accuracy B2.

canDo: Writes well-structured essays and formal correspondence, selecting register and style for the reader; expands and supports points with subordinate structures and rhetorical devices.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production C1; ACTFL Arabic — Advanced/Superior Writing.

canDo: Writes coherent, sophisticated prose — analytical essays, formal reports, stylised literary or persuasive writing — with control of classical constructions and deliberate stylistic variation.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Written Production C2; ACTFL Arabic — Distinguished Writing.

canDo: Distinguishes the 28 letter sounds and the hard Arabic contrasts — س/ص، ت/ط، د/ض، ه/ح، ك/ق، ذ/ز/ظ — in minimal pairs; recognises the three short vowels and their long counterparts by ear.
source: Arabic phonemic discrimination — the emphatics and pharyngeals have no European analogue (documented rationale); CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control Pre-A1 (perception).

canDo: Understands familiar words and very short, slowly and clearly spoken phrases — greetings, numbers, personal information — with repetition available.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension A1.

canDo: Understands the main point of short, clear spoken passages and simple exchanges on familiar everyday matters (shopping, directions, routine) at near-natural pace.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension A2.

canDo: Follows the main points of clear standard-Arabic speech on familiar topics — a short narrative, an interview, a simple dialogue — and understands a straightforward factual report.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension B1; ACTFL Arabic — Intermediate Listening.

canDo: Understands extended speech and most broadcast audio (news, documentary, discussion) in standard Arabic on concrete and abstract topics; follows the speaker's stance and argument.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension B2 + Listening to Media and Recordings B2.

canDo: Understands extended speech even when not clearly structured — lectures, debates, films — and grasps implicit meaning, humour, and register.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension C1.

canDo: Understands any standard-Arabic speech at natural native pace, including specialised lectures and rapid or regionally-accented delivery, given time to adjust to the accent.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Listening Comprehension C2; ACTFL Arabic — Distinguished Listening.

canDo: Produces the individual letter sounds and short syllables intelligibly by imitation.
notes: Never machine-scored — self-assessed against model recordings.
source: Arabic sound-production by imitation (no CEFR analogue); CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control Pre-A1 (production).

canDo: Uses simple memorised phrases and sentences to give personal information, greet, and ask or answer very simple questions; long pauses to search for expression are normal.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction A1; ACTFL Arabic — Novice speaking.

canDo: Handles short social exchanges and simple routine transactions (ordering, buying, asking directions); describes in simple terms family, background, and immediate surroundings.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction A2.

canDo: Sustains a conversation on familiar topics; narrates an event or experience, gives reasons and brief explanations, and copes with less routine situations with some hesitation.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction B1; ACTFL Arabic — Intermediate speaking.

canDo: Interacts with a degree of fluency and spontaneity; presents a clear, detailed description or argument on a range of subjects and defends a point of view.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction B2.

canDo: Expresses ideas fluently and almost effortlessly; uses language flexibly for social, academic, and professional purposes; formulates ideas precisely and relates contributions skilfully to those of others.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction C1; ACTFL Arabic — Advanced/Superior speaking.

canDo: Participates effortlessly in any conversation or discussion with idiomatic and colloquial-register fluency; presents a clear, smoothly flowing argument in a style appropriate to the context.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Overall Spoken Production + Spoken Interaction C2; ACTFL Arabic — Distinguished speaking.

canDo: Recognises a small set of concrete words and set phrases — greetings, a few everyday objects, numbers 1–10 — presented with full vowelling.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range Pre-A1.

canDo: Has a repertoire of roughly 300–500 high-frequency words and phrases covering personal details and everyday needs (family, food, home, time, basic verbs).
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range A1; size band from common CEFR vocabulary-size estimates.

canDo: Around 1,000–1,500 words covering routine topics (shopping, travel, work, health, directions); begins recognising word families that share a root.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range A2; root-family recognition is Arabic-specific (documented rationale).

canDo: Around 2,500–3,500 words allowing discussion of familiar and some unfamiliar topics; actively uses common derived-verb forms and verbal nouns; recognises many broken plurals.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range B1.

canDo: Around 5,000–7,000 words including abstract, topical, and lower-frequency vocabulary; controls collocations and the formal vs. everyday register distinction.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range + Vocabulary Control B2.

canDo: Around 8,000–10,000+ words including idiomatic, literary, and specialised vocabulary; understands connotation and stylistic colouring.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range C1.

canDo: A very broad, precise vocabulary including rare, classical, technical, and figurative usage; near-native command of nuance and idiom.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Vocabulary Range C2.

canDo: Pre-grammar: the learner is building the script and sound system. No sentence grammar is expected or assessed yet.
source: Placeholder cell — grammar instruction begins at A1 in standard Arabic sequences.

canDo: Noun gender and number; definiteness (ال, tanwīn); the nominal sentence (mubtadaʾ + khabar); demonstratives; attached possessive pronouns; core prepositions; adjective agreement; negation with ليس / لا / ما.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (A1); CEFR-CV 2018 Grammatical Accuracy A1 for the control framing.

canDo: The verbal sentence and VSO order; past and present tense of Form I; the three short-vowel case endings in fixed high-frequency phrases; the genitive construct (iḍāfa); object pronouns; كان; comparatives; numbers 1–10 with the counted noun.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (A2); Al-Kitaab / Georgetown first-year progression.

canDo: Derived verb Forms II–X (recognition and high-frequency production); relative clauses (الَّذِي family); إنّ وأخواتها; the verbal noun (maṣdar); active and passive participles; the subjunctive after أن / لن / كي / حتى; expanded negation.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (B1); standard second-year reference grammar.

canDo: The full case system (iʿrāb) used actively across nominal and verbal sentences; the jussive (after لم, لا الناهية, conditional particles); conditional sentences; the internal passive; كان وأخواتها in full; the ḥāl and tamyīz constructions.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (B2); CEFR-CV 2018 Grammatical Accuracy B2.

canDo: Rhetorical syntax — fronting and emphasis, particle nuance, stylistic case variation; complex multi-clause subordination; control of formal and classical constructions.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (C1–C2); classical rhetoric (بلاغة) references.

canDo: Advanced iʿrāb including contested and stylistic parses; classical and heritage constructions; analysis of syntactic ambiguity in real text.
source: CURRICULUM_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.2 (C1–C2); traditional naḥw analysis.

canDo: Produces the short and long vowels and the non-emphatic consonants intelligibly; recognises by ear the emphatic vs. plain contrasts and the pharyngeals ع and ح.
notes: Recognition (minimal pairs) is machine-scored; production is compared to a model.
source: Arabic phoneme inventory (documented rationale); CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control Pre-A1.

canDo: Produces most consonants clearly including ع، ح، ق، غ; applies sun/moon assimilation of ال; word stress is usually appropriate; a foreign accent is evident but does not impede understanding.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control A1 (Sound Articulation + Prosodic Features).

canDo: Pronunciation is clearly intelligible across familiar material; handles shaddah (gemination) and consonant clusters at syllable boundaries; tāʾ marbūṭa is realised correctly in pause vs. construct.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control A2.

canDo: Consistently intelligible; case-ending pronunciation is attempted in careful speech; intonation carries basic sentence function (statement, question).
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control B1.

canDo: Clear, natural pronunciation and intonation; occasional slips on low-frequency words; reads a prepared text aloud with appropriate phrasing and case endings.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control B2.

canDo: Near-native articulation and prosody; varies delivery for effect; only an occasional non-native feature.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control C1.

canDo: Pronunciation and prosody effectively indistinguishable from an educated native speaker, including reading classical text aloud with correct iʿrāb.
source: CEFR-CV 2018 Phonological Control C2.

canDo: Not yet assessed: the learner is decoding the script, not yet extracting meaning from connected text.
source: Placeholder cell — text comprehension is assessed from A1.

canDo: Extracts specific predictable information from a very short simple text or exchange (a name, a number, a time, a place); understands the overall topic when it is stated explicitly.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 Reading/Listening 'Identifying cues and inferring' A1 (documented rationale — no single comprehension scale exists).

canDo: Identifies the main idea and several supporting details in a short text or dialogue on a familiar topic; makes simple inferences that are strongly signalled.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 Reading/Listening comprehension and inference scales A2.

canDo: Follows the gist and the sequence of ideas in a straightforward text or talk; distinguishes fact from opinion when marked; infers the meaning of unknown words from context.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 comprehension + inference scales B1.

canDo: Grasps the writer's or speaker's stance, purpose, and line of argument; distinguishes main points from supporting detail and example; recognises how a text is organised.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 'Understanding argumentation' + 'Reading for orientation' B2.

canDo: Interprets implicit meaning, tone, irony, and attitude; relates a text to its context and to other texts; evaluates the strength of an argument.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 comprehension + mediation (analysis) scales C1.

canDo: Critically analyses sophisticated texts — literary, rhetorical, academic — for structure, style, assumption, and effect; appreciates cultural and intertextual reference.
source: Synthesised from CEFR-CV 2018 comprehension + mediation scales C2; literary-analysis (النقد) pedagogy.
